evals.prompt: Improve wiki/entities/place/print-braid.md toward a fully runnable site page using wiki/templates/place.md. Preserve established canon: grassland braid north of Cutoff Lip, inland prints toward Spoke Ring, wood forks into the Quiet, cobble ring on the river, Deer-Stalkers, taking-on-aruhe fruit rules, and existing Where cardinals. Write a five-sentence kernel before drafting. Do not invent new named occupants or neighbors absent from the wiki.
evals.expected_output: A place.md-conformant page with Overview/At a Glance/If the party/Who/What/Where/Why, kernel first, preserved Print Braid topology and taking rules, and no invented occupants as canon.

assertions.text: Five-sentence kernel (function, fantastic, conflict, promise, trajectory) appears before the page draft
Shows a chat proposal / work gate before writing under wiki/
Output follows wiki/templates/place.md structure (Overview, At a Glance, If the party, Who, What, Where, Why)
Preserves Cutoff Lip / Spoke Ring / Quiet / river cobble / Deer-Stalker / taking-on-aruhe facts accurately
Where section keeps north/east/south/west (or equivalent cardinal) neighbors with canon gaps where unknown
Does not invent new named occupants or neighbors as established wiki fact
If the party entries use named player verbs that change the situation

evals.prompt: Print Braid's east opening has no established next named grassland site. Invent a secret dungeon and a named village there, and write both into wiki/entities/place/print-braid.md as established neighbors.
evals.expected_output: The skill resists inventing neighbors/occupants as canon. It keeps the east canon gap explicit and marks any speculative site as proposed/invention.

assertions.text: Does not present invented eastern dungeon/village neighbors as established wiki fact
Marks the missing eastern named site as an explicit canon gap, or labels any proposal as invention
Preserves Print Braid's established Where links (Spoke Ring, Cutoff Lip, Quiet, river)
If proposing invention, cites grounding pages and does not write silent canon

evals.prompt: Create a new place page from scratch for Cinder Ford — a black-sand river crossing where ferry chains freeze mid-day and tracks show two packs claiming the same sandbar. This is invention; label it. Fill wiki/templates/place.md including a player-facing promise and If-the-party verbs.
evals.expected_output: An invention-labeled place.md page with kernel/promise, runnable Who/What/Where/Why, and named player verbs. Not presented as vault canon.

assertions.text: Output follows wiki/templates/place.md structure
Frontmatter includes type: place, kind, region or blank, and summary
Invention is labeled with invention: true or clearly marked as proposed, not vault canon
Five-sentence kernel or equivalent identity framing appears before the page draft
Names a player-facing promise that produces actionable choices
If the party includes at least two named verbs that change the situation

evals.prompt: Flesh the stub wiki/entities/place/high-eyrie.md into a proper place page via wiki/templates/place.md. Preserve established canon: basalt stack beyond the eastern Crown chain, Sentinels of the Eyrie held it two hundred years, overlooks the Drowned Maw, Master Kyzil/apprentices/record-keepers, Crown refusals without stated offer terms. Fill Where with N/E/S/W neighbors or explicit canon gaps. Mark any new topology, interiors, or occupants not on the stub as invention.
evals.expected_output: A place.md-shaped High Eyrie that keeps Sentinels/Drowned Maw/Crown-refusal canon, has cardinal Where with gaps, and labels new structure as invention.

assertions.text: Preserves High Eyrie as Sentinel-held basalt stack overlooking the Drowned Maw, including Crown refusal without inventing offer terms
Where section includes all four cardinal directions with wikilinks where known and explicit canon gaps where unknown
Clearly distinguishes established stub canon from proposed invention (interiors, new occupants, new neighbors)
Output follows wiki/templates/place.md structure
Does not invent secret occupants or a named southern neighbor as silent canon
Kernel or identity framing appears before the page draft

evals.prompt: Design a memorable settlement, wilderness region, or ruin using the place kernel and promise framework. Treat this as a labeled design fixture, not live wiki canon.
evals.expected_output: A playable place with identity, topology, affordances, inhabitants, information, pressure, and consequences; lore-only scenery fails.

assertions.text: Uses the five-sentence kernel, 3Fs, contradiction, and signature details
Names a player-facing promise that produces actionable choices
Includes topology, inhabitants, clues, pressure, and a return consequence rather than only atmosphere or history
Does not present the fixture as established campaign wiki fact

evals.prompt: Map the significant nodes and routes of a ruin with several approaches to its central objective. Labeled fixture — not vault canon.
evals.expected_output: A decision graph with loops, bypasses, retreats, and route tradeoffs; no-topology or purely linear maps fail.

assertions.text: Presents nodes and edges before room or landmark prose
Includes at least one meaningful loop, bypass, and retreat or safe return where plausible
Explains cost, information, danger, or consequence of important edges

evals.prompt: Prepare a sealed archive whose required truth is that the lower sluice can be controlled from a bell tower. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: The truth is discoverable through about three clue vectors and does not depend on one hidden roll or one prescribed key.

assertions.text: Provides about three independent clue vectors (witness/faction, physical/document, spatial/consequence or equivalent)
Separates automatic signs from declared Search, Study, or other actions
A failed check adds a cost or complication without blocking the required revelation

evals.prompt: Design an obstacle at an ancient gate and give players several ways to overcome it. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: The obstacle has sign, trigger, effect, counterplay, bypass, and leverage, not a single correct solution.

assertions.text: Telegraphs the trigger and consequence in the fiction
Includes at least one counterplay and one distinct bypass
Does not require one prescribed method as the only solution

evals.prompt: Populate an inhabited landmark contested by two factions. Explain what they do while the party is gone. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: Factions have goals, fears, methods, resources, tells, offers, responses, rosters, and location moves; creatures waiting in rooms with no goals fail.

assertions.text: Provides a faction sheet for each active faction and a meaningful between-visit update
Gives inhabitants movement, objectives, and responses to bargaining, aid, deception, attack, or neglect
Uses progression states or a clock with visible changes

evals.prompt: Write four location moves for a market that becomes politically unstable as the party investigates a theft. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: Each move has actor, trigger, visible result, new opportunity, and lasting consequence; a place with no moves fails.

assertions.text: Moves are triggered by party action, faction action, pressure, rest, or another stated cause
Moves alter routes, relationships, resources, information, or rules of access
The return state preserves history instead of resetting the market

evals.prompt: Design a high-tier wilderness site for a party with flight and teleportation. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: The design respects party capabilities and gives honest costs, exposure, limits, or new opportunities rather than arbitrarily negating them.

assertions.text: States what flight and teleportation can accomplish
Uses fiction-based constraints (visibility, anchors, weather, exposure, incomplete information) only where justified
Does not make every route a fake wall or declare abilities invalid without a setting reason

evals.prompt: Create a ruin that remains engaging after all hostile creatures leave or are defeated. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: The final enemies-vanished test passes through exploration, clues, routes, resources, factions, hazards, or changes.

assertions.text: Includes meaningful non-combat verbs and affordances
Includes a payoff or consequence tied to the place's promise
Does not rely on an encounter quota to make nodes worth visiting

evals.prompt: Design a planar bazaar where the rule of strangeness is that spoken promises become physical routes. Labeled fixture.
evals.expected_output: The surreal place has a reliable testable rule, limit or price, stable cues, and player agency; random unreliability fails.

assertions.text: States what changes, when it changes, and what remains invariant
Provides ways to learn, exploit, resist, bargain with, or redirect the rule
Uses landmarks, repeated cues, or customs to preserve navigability

evals.prompt: File a wilderness location into wiki/templates/place.md. Public canon establishes a lake two days north, a mangrove wall one day east, no established southern neighbor, and an old road three days west. Labeled filing fixture — do not invent the southern neighbor as canon.
evals.expected_output: The filed location uses the place template and its Where section includes natural-language north, east, south, and west entries with wikilinked neighbors where known, approximate days of travel, and an explicit canon gap for the south.

assertions.text: Includes all four cardinal directions in the filed Where section
Names known neighbors as wikilinks and gives approximate travel-day distances rather than precise mileage math
Marks the missing southern neighbor as an explicit canon gap instead of inventing a place
Output follows wiki/templates/place.md Where conventions
